sources.title: Protein and amino acid requirements in human nutrition: report of a joint WHO/FAO/UNU expert consultation (WHO Technical Report Series 935)
Dietary Reference Intakes for Energy, Carbohydrate, Fiber, Fat, Fatty Acids, Cholesterol, Protein, and Amino Acids

concepts.definition: A molecule with an amino group, a carboxyl group, a hydrogen and a side chain on one carbon.
An amino acid the body cannot make in sufficient amounts, so it must come from food.
The essential amino acid in shortest supply in a protein relative to human need.
Leucine, isoleucine and valine, which have branched side chains.

questions.a: Proteins and most enzymes use the L form of amino acids; the label names the form found in the body.

questions.q: Why does rice with beans give better protein quality than either alone?
questions.a: Rice is limited in lysine and beans in sulfur amino acids, so together they complement each other.
